name: Reaper Farm rfUSDC vault redeem without owner authorisation
summary: ReaperVaultV2 exposes the three-argument ERC-4626 exit path redeem(shares, receiver, owner) (and the matching withdraw) but never checks that msg.sender is owner or holds an allowance from owner, so any caller could burn an arbitrary holder’s vault shares and have the underlying asset paid to an address of their choosing. The attacker contract called redeem with each depositor as owner and its own address as receiver; the three owners drained in the anchor transaction had an allowance of exactly 0 to the attacker contract at block 44045360.
notes: The vault is a plain non-upgradeable deployment: eth_getCode is empty at blocks 41839238 and 41839239 and 16,821 bytes from block 41839240, and keccak(eth_getCode) is 0xd056c916021b116be7449251fe457147d6fcdc124a4a4fa604e271054ad0f085 at the creation block and unchanged at blocks 41900000, 42500000, 43000000, 43500000, 44000000 and 44045360, which is also the code hash the prestateTracer reports inside the anchor transaction. The EIP-1967 implementation, beacon and admin slots and the legacy OpenZeppelin implementation slot all read zero at block 44045360, and the anchor trace contains no DELEGATECALL out of the vault, so no proxy or module indirection supplies its code.

Scoped to the rfUSDC vault 0xcda5dea176f2df95082f4dadb96255bdb2bc7c7d, the only Reaper vault that executes in the anchor transaction. Its Withdraw(caller,receiver,owner,assets,shares) log stream from creation to block 44060000 contains 13 events with caller != owner attributable to the attacker, spread over three transactions at blocks 44045361, 44045487 and 44045900, and their assets sum to exactly 596,685.496653 USDC; the attacker receiver 0x2c177d20b1b1d68cc85d3215904a7bb6629ca954 bridged out that exact amount (596685496653 units) at block 44046708 in transaction 0x73a62117b6b88dc6e8384dce596392f995f1f37a10f6dc05f4bbf881e4be6bc5. The 14 later third-party redeems on the same vault (blocks 44052039-44053339, caller 0x1e71aee6081f62053123140aacc7a06021d77348, receiver the safe 0x539ef36c804e4d735d8cab69e8e441c12d4b88e0, about 25,600 USDC) are a rescue sweep of the remaining balances and are excluded; that receiver has made no outbound transfer. The same campaign also drained the sibling vaults rfETH 0x58c60b6df933ff5615890ddddcdd280bad53f1c1, rfWFTM 0xa6313302b3ceff2727f19aaa30d7240d5b3cd9cd, rfBTC 0xeb7761d05a31769d35073f703dd3a41f3ca9bd3d, rfDAI 0x77dc33dc0278d21398cb9b16cbff99c1b712a87a and rfUSDT 0xa9a9db466685f977f9ecee347958bcef90498177, which brings the widely reported campaign total to about USD 1.7M; those vaults are separate deployments with distinct runtime code hashes, none of them executes in this anchor transaction, and their value is not counted here.
